# Intake Brief — Power-up level gym demonstration and game/gym parity tests (AH-0MUV5CLVQ006V9HR)

## Headline

Add a dedicated, auto-discovered `GymPowerUpLeveling` demonstration scene that makes every power-up's (P3–P10) run-scoped level curve observable — field pickups and hold-full permanent rewards both level the power-up up, and a live readout shows the resolver-derived stats — plus integration and game↔gym parity tests that boot the real gym and assert the shared power-up level path is byte-for-byte the same in `PlayScene` and the gyms.

## Problem statement

The power-up level model, resolver and store are shipped (`src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`, parent AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6) and wired into the shared effect path and every scene (AH-0MUV5CLW6005VF7K, AH-0MUVM9RAO004Y3LB, AH-0MUV5CLVO002ZHS9), but there is **no dedicated place to see and verify it** the way weapons have `GymWeaponLeveling`. The existing power-up gyms (`GymPowerUpsCombat`, `GymPowerUpsUtility`) demonstrate behaviours, not levels; the parity tests in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` boot a *minimal* `EquivGymScene`, not a real gym, and only exercise a single power-up (P5). There is therefore a gap in both **legibility** (a producer/designer cannot watch a power-up level up and see its stats change) and **verification** (no test proves a shipped gym resolves the level path identically to the game).

## Users

- **Designer / producer (legibility):** "As a designer, I want a gym where I can collect a power-up repeatedly and watch its level and resolved stats change, so I can sanity-check the curve without reading the catalogue."
- **Engineer (verification):** "As an engineer, I want a test that boots the real gym and the game and proves they resolve the same level path for every power-up, so a divergent copy cannot slip through."
- **Player (indirect):** "As a player, I want the power-up levels I earn to be applied identically everywhere they appear, with no gym-only behaviour."

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — Dedicated gym scene.** A new `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts` (scene key `GymPowerUpLeveling`, conventional `Gym<Name>.ts` so it is auto-discovered by `GymIndex` with no index edit) demonstrates the level curve of **every** power-up P3–P10: the operator can collect each power-up repeatedly (field drops) and take a hold-full permanent reward, and the scene shows the current run-scoped level plus the resolver-derived stats for all catalogue variables, updating visibly as the level rises.
- **AC2 — No duplicated model.** The gym reads levels and stats only through the shared `PowerUpLevelStore` / `resolvePowerUpAtLevel` (and `EffectsRegistry`); it defines no copy of the curve, the catalogue or the level arithmetic, and introduces no new shared helper or template-method copy (the duplicate-body guard in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` continues to pass).
- **AC3 — Integration tests.** `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.test.ts` drives the scene deterministically and verifies: field-pickup leveling, hold-full permanent leveling, the level readout matches `resolvePowerUpAtLevel` at representative levels (base / first upgrade / mid / cap), every P3–P10 has a growing axis, and the level resets only on run restart.
- **AC4 — Game↔gym parity.** Tests boot the real `GymPowerUpLeveling` alongside `PlayScene` and assert that, for every power-up P3–P10 across a level sweep (0, 1, mid, cap), the run-scoped level, the resolved stats and the observable effect-path outputs (e.g. P5 speed multiplier, P8 lives, P3 absorptions, P7 teleports, P9/P10 stack caps) are identical. The parity assertion lives in the shared equivalence test (or a sibling parity test) so the duplicate-body guard convention is respected.
- **AC5 — Documentation.** The GDD §4.4.3 status paragraph, the README power-up leveling entry and the "Coverage:" lists name the new gym and its tests (and any code comments added are accurate).
- **AC6 — Full suite.** The full project test suite passes with the new changes (CI/CD pipeline tests are out of scope).

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md).** An enabled gameplay object must run the same code in a gym and the game; any behaviour shared by game and gym lives once in `src/scenes/core/` and is consumed by both. No divergent copy.
- **Demonstration only.** This item adds a scene and tests; it must **not** change gameplay balance, tuning or the level catalogue. Any balance change discovered is a separate linked work item, not scope creep.
- **Auto-discovery convention.** New gym is `src/scenes/gym/Gym<Name>.ts`; the scene key equals the class name.
- **Deterministic tests.** Scene tests use the `bootScene` harness and the public `tick(dt)` entry point (no real render loop), matching the existing gym tests; generous Vitest timeouts are acceptable for Phaser boot.
- **UK English** in all code comments, docs and work-item text.

## Existing state

- **Model shipped:** `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS` (all P3–P10), pure `resolvePowerUpAtLevel`, `summarisePowerUpLevelChange`, run-scoped `PowerUpLevelStore` on `Player` (`getPowerUpLevel`, `getPowerUpLevels`, `resetPowerUpLevels`), shared curve in `src/utils/curve.ts`.
- **Effect path wired:** `EffectsRegistry.applyCollect` consumes the player's store; P3 `shieldAbsorptions` and P4 `bombRange`/`bombFrequency` axes wired; hold-full `ChoiceContext.powerUpLevels` + `power-up-level` offers applied via shared `applyMineralChoiceReward`.
- **Precedent:** `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts` (+ `.test.ts`) is the weapon-leveling demonstration gym (parent AH-0MUQOXHWT000XV4J); `GymIndex` auto-discovers gyms; `GymCurveSequencer` shows the DOM-panel readout pattern.
- **Existing power-up gyms:** `GymPowerUpsCombat` (P3/P4/P6/P7, threats) and `GymPowerUpsUtility` (P5/P8/P9/P10, threat-free) demonstrate behaviour, not levels; neither shows a level/stat readout.
- **Existing partial parity:** `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` boots a minimal `EquivGymScene` and checks P5 only; `PlayScene.powerUpLevels.test.ts` covers the choice path in the game.
- **HUD** (`src/ui/HUD.ts`) renders weapon levels but has no power-up level readout.

## Desired change

Add `GymPowerUpLeveling` (auto-discovered) as the canonical place to observe every power-up's level curve, showing level and resolver-derived stats; add integration tests for field-pickup and hold-full leveling, the readout and run-restart reset; and add game↔gym parity tests that boot the real gym and assert the shared level path matches `PlayScene` for every power-up. Update the GDD/README references accordingly. No gameplay behaviour changes.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts` — **new** demonstration gym scene: round-robin/level-up drop source for P3–P10, hold-full permanent path, and a level + resolved-stats readout (reusing the shared store/resolver).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.test.ts` — **new** integration tests (field pickup, permanent reward, readout vs resolver, reset-on-restart, every-power-up-has-an-axis).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — extend (or add a sibling real-gym parity test) to boot `GymPowerUpLeveling` and assert `PlayScene`↔gym identity across every power-up and a level sweep; keeps the duplicate-body guard authoritative.
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — **read-only** shared source of truth (`POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS`, `resolvePowerUpAtLevel`, `PowerUpLevelStore`); do not duplicate.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — shared effect path consumed by the gym (read-only).
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — only if a power-up level readout is added to the shared HUD; otherwise the readout stays gym-local (e.g. a `.gym-panel`).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4.3 — update the status/coverage sentence to name the shipped gym + tests.
- `README.md` — update the power-up leveling entry and its Coverage list.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk (primary):** a demo gym invites "while we're here" gameplay or tuning changes. Mitigation: this item is demonstration + tests only; record any balance/behaviour opportunity as a separate `discovered-from` item.
- **Threats vs legibility (assumption):** P3/P4/P6/P7 are only fully observable under threat; the demonstration gym may include an optional threat toggle **or** focus on the resolver/level readout and leave full combat behaviour to `GymPowerUpsCombat`. Chosen default: threat-free readout gallery, with an optional threat toggle only if needed for the parity tests.
- **HUD coupling (assumption):** the shared HUD has no power-up level readout; keep the new readout gym-local to avoid changing shared HUD behaviour.
- **Parity-test flakiness (risk):** booting two Phaser games per case under parallel load is slow; reuse the existing generous timeout pattern and a single level sweep per power-up rather than many boots.
- **Reset-on-run-restart (ambiguity):** the gym must offer a deterministic way to exercise `resetPowerUpLevels` for the reset test; expose a public restart/reset hook (test-only seam) rather than relying on a real GameOver.
- **Determinism (constraint):** all tests drive `tick(dt)`, no wall-clock.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6** — Design level curves for all power-ups (parent / `discovered-from`). Ships the model this gym demonstrates.
- **AH-0MUV5CLW6005VF7K** — Wire power-up level curves into `EffectsRegistry` and the shared effect path (predecessor; makes field pickups level up).
- **AH-0MUVM9RAO004Y3LB** — Wire P3 shield absorption and P4 periodic bomb (range/frequency) level axes into the effect path.
- **AH-0MUV5CLVO002ZHS9** — Integrate power-up level-up offers into the hold-full choice.
- **AH-0MUWGD0EN008T3TY** — P4 model: `bombRange`/`bombFrequency` replace `bombCharges` (supersedes the original P4 axis).
- **AH-0MUQOXHWT000XV4J** — Weapon-leveling gym demonstration + integration tests (the direct structural precedent; mirrors the same shape for weapons).
- **AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA** — Gym↔game behavioural parity: eliminate remaining core-code duplication (the parity convention this item must respect).
- **AH-0MUTPEIN0000MDUR** — Test: P10 parity across `PlayScene`, `GymMinerals` and `GymPowerUpsUtility` (precedent for real-gym parity tests).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MTHG5B83007W4W4** – Single reusable enemy gym scene (GymEnemies) (completed)
- **AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K** – Retune the default difficulty curve and seed campaign for playability (completed)
- **AH-0MU44MAAB0007BDD** – Documentation for combat spawning (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: 0muu2qje2007jnr6, add, applies, assert, body (+23 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: add, applies, assert, body, combatscene (+20 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0muu2qje2007jnr6, add, applies, body, combatscene (+20 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive interview round was conducted: the seed context plus the shipped model, the wiring predecessors and the `GymWeaponLeveling` precedent were sufficient to draft a clear brief (intake SKILL §4 — skip the interview when seed context suffices; AGENTS.md — do not ask unnecessary questions). Each apparent design choice is recorded below with the evidence that resolved it and the documented assumption taken where evidence was partial.

- **Q (resolved from the work item + precedent): Should this be a new dedicated gym or an extension of `GymPowerUpsCombat` / `GymPowerUpsUtility`?** — Answer: a **new** `GymPowerUpLeveling` scene. Evidence: the work-item title and description say "Add a gym scene"; the `GymWeaponLeveling` precedent (AH-0MUQOXHWT000XV4J) established a dedicated leveling gym; `GymIndex` auto-discovers `Gym<Name>.ts`. Source: work-item description; `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts`; `src/utils/gymDiscovery.ts`.
- **Q (resolved from the work item): What is the parity-test scope?** — Answer: boot the **real** gym and assert the shared power-up level path is identical to `PlayScene`, not another minimal `EquivGymScene`. Evidence: the description explicitly requires game↔gym parity "for the shared power-up level path" and names the duplicate-body guard. Source: work-item description; `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`.
- **Q (assumption recorded): Should the gym include combat threats so P3/P4/P6/P7 behaviour is fully observable?** — Answer (assumed, producer may override): threat-free readout gallery as the default, with an optional threat toggle only if the parity tests require observable combat behaviour. Evidence: `GymWeaponLeveling` is threat-free and demonstrates levels via a readout; `GymPowerUpsCombat` already owns the threat-based P3/P4/P6/P7 behaviour. Source: `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts`.
- **Q (assumption recorded): What demonstrates "level" — a shared HUD readout or a gym-local panel?** — Answer (assumed): gym-local readout over `PowerUpLevelStore` / `resolvePowerUpAtLevel`; avoid changing shared HUD behaviour. Evidence: the shared HUD has only a weapon-level readout; `GymCurveSequencer` shows the established gym-local `.gym-panel` pattern. Source: `src/ui/HUD.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymCurveSequencer.ts`.
- **Q (assumption recorded): How does the gym exercise level reset?** — Answer (assumed): expose a deterministic public restart/reset hook on the gym scene so the reset test does not depend on a real GameOver sequence. Source: `Player.getPowerUpLevels` / `resetPowerUpLevels` (`src/entities/Player.ts`).
- **Observation:** the automated `find-related` report surfaced only generic matches (enemy gym, difficulty curve, combat-spawning docs); the higher-signal relationships above were found by manual worklog search and file inspection.

## Plan: changelog

- **2026-10-14:** Plan skill executed. Decomposed into 3 children:
  1. AH-0MV7QKEEO006WFI1 — Implement GymPowerUpLeveling gym scene with integration tests (covers parent AC1–AC3)
  2. AH-0MV7QSZMW009OA75 — Game↔gym parity tests for the power-up level path (covers parent AC4)
  3. AH-0MV7QVOAG003U8AA — Document the GymPowerUpLeveling gym and verify the full suite (covers parent AC5–AC6)
- Dependency edges: parity depends on gym, docs depends on gym.
- Effort/risk: Small / Medium, score 6. Recommended 20.17h.
- Six automated review stages passed.
- AC coverage: all 6 parent ACs covered by children (see comment AH-C0MV7T60R9009Z2BR for matcher false-negative analysis).
- Four spurious auto-closed gap children (AH-0MV7SM4IX003WMAB, AH-0MV7SM4VS001GEWJ, AH-0MV7SM57F009S6QL, AH-0MV7SM5IA006OE9S) closed as duplicates.
- Parent stage set to `plan_complete`, status `open`.
data.title: Power-up level gym demonstration and game/gym parity tests

## Goal
Remove the now-unused `'onImpact'` AOE projectile-detonation machinery (dead code retained by AH-0MUUF9GZV004WVT9) and its tests, now that no catalogue weapon uses the `'onImpact'` trigger.

## Context
AH-0MUUF9GZV004WVT9 moved the Mortar from `'onImpact'` to `'onRandom'`, so the `'onImpact'` path is no longer referenced by any weapon definition. Per project dead-code discipline it was deliberately retained during that change; this item is the follow-up cleanup (discovered-from:AH-0MUUF9GZV004WVT9).

## Scope (in)
- `src/utils/weapons.ts`: drop `'onImpact'` from the `AoETrigger` union; remove the `onImpact` descriptor doc; remove `AOE_PROJECTILE_SPEEDS` if it has no remaining consumer (the Mortar's range basis is to be made explicit separately if needed).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`: remove the `onAoeProjectileSpawned` hook and the `'onImpact'` branch in `_autoFire` (bullet spawn is then only unreachable; decide whether projectile spawn remains for any weapon).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`: remove `onAoeProjectileSpawned`, `detonateAoeProjectile`, the `bullet.aoeWeapon` handling in `onPlayerBulletHitsEnemy`, and the mortar VFX/sound path from `spawnAoeDetonationVfx` if unused.
- `src/entities/PlayerBullet.ts`: remove `aoeWeapon`, `aoeDetonated`, `onExpire` (if only used by the AOE path) and their comments.
- `src/scenes/core/AoeWeapons.test.ts`: remove the retained `onImpact` tests (the section marked 'Retained onImpact projectile-detonation machinery (dead code)').
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`: remove `onAoeProjectileSpawned`/`detonateAoeProjectile` from `SHARED_AOE_METHODS`.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`: update the descriptor union text (remove `'onImpact'`) and any remaining onImpact references.

## Out of scope
- Any behavioural change to Nova, Mortar or Arc.
- Removing the generic player-bullet spawn path used by conventional weapons.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1 — `AoETrigger` is `'onFire' | 'onRandom'`; no source references `'onImpact'` remain (except historical docs/changelog if intentionally kept — enumerate any).
- [ ] AC2 — The onImpact hooks/methods and `PlayerBullet` AOE fields are removed, and `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean.
- [ ] AC3 — The retained-onImpact tests are removed; `AoeWeapons.test.ts` still covers Nova/Arc/Mortar random detonation.
- [ ] AC4 — Gym↔game parity guard (`CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) still passes with the reduced `SHARED_AOE_METHODS`.
- [ ] AC5 — Docs (`docs/Game Design Document.md`) still pass `src/aoeDocs.test.ts` (or are updated if the guard references removed strings).
- [ ] AC6 — Full suite green (`/skill:test`).

## Notes / risks
- `spawnAoeDetonationVfx` (Mortar burst + cue, off-screen culling) is still needed by the `'onRandom'` path — do not remove it.
- The generic `spawnPlayerBullet` path must remain for the cannon/spread/dual/rapid.
- If any consumer of `AOE_PROJECTILE_SPEEDS` remains as the Mortar range basis, either keep it (renamed/documented) or replace the range basis explicitly; do not silently drop the Mortar range.

# Halve bulletSpeed in unknown-archetype fallbacks

## Problem statement

AH-0MUWZ5GST003NMFQ halves the enemy `bulletSpeed` of the eight shipped archetypes
across the runtime CSV, `DEFAULT_ENEMY_CONFIGS` and the per-entity constants.
During planning, three additional runtime fallbacks were found that also hard-code
`bulletSpeed: 200` for **unknown** archetype keys and were explicitly out of that
item's scope (its Q2 enumeration covered only CSV + defaults + entity constants):

- `src/core/configStore.ts` — `genericEnemyDefault()`
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` — `resolveBaseConfig()`
- `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts` — `groupEnemyConfig()`

Leaving them at 200 means an unknown-key enemy would fire at double the speed of
every shipped archetype, so tuning can still drift for that edge case.

## Desired change

Decide and, if accepted, halve these three `bulletSpeed` fallbacks (200 → 100) for
consistency, updating any affected difficulty-sequencer expectations.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 — The three unknown-archetype fallbacks use `bulletSpeed: 100` (or a
  documented decision is recorded to leave them at 200 with rationale).
- [ ] AC2 — Any difficulty-sequencer or difficulty-scoring test affected by the
  change is updated and the full suite passes.
- [ ] AC3 — The decision and rationale are recorded on this item.

## Key Files

- `src/core/configStore.ts`
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts`
- `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts`

## Related work

- AH-0MUWZ5GST003NMFQ — Reduce bullet speed of enemies (parent discovery; strictly out of its scope).

Raised during intake of AH-0MUX802450085VZZ (field pickups must upgrade temporarily). The producer asked us to *consider creating a second power-up type* to represent consumable temporary grants (P6 Phase Shift charges, P7 Teleport stacks) whose unconsumed grants persist until consumed even after the temporary level window expires.

**discovered-from:AH-0MUX802450085VZZ**

## Goal
Evaluate whether consumable temporary grants should be modelled as a distinct power-up type/category rather than as a level that is temporarily raised. This is an *exploratory* task — no code behaviour change is committed until a design decision is made and accepted.

## Acceptance criteria
- A short design note is recorded on this item comparing (a) the level-based temporary model chosen in AH-0MUX802450085VZZ vs (b) a distinct consumable-grant type.
- Recommendation (with rationale) is recorded and the producing work item is linked.
- If a change is recommended, follow-up implementation work items are created; otherwise the item is closed as 'no change required'.

## Notes
- This item is NOT blocking AH-0MUX802450085VZZ, which proceeds with decision (b): unconsumed grants persist until consumed and are not removed on expiry.
data.title: Consider a distinct power-up type for consumable temporary grants (P6/P7)

# Report script counts soft-deleted children

**discovered-from:AH-0MUZMTTYH008KVS2**

## Problem

The canonical end-of-session report (`skill/report/scripts/render_report.py`) shows an incorrect **Children** count when a parent has soft-deleted children.

- `wl delete <id>` is a **soft delete** — it sets `status=deleted` and `deletedBy`, and the item remains visible via `wl show <parent> --children`.
- `wl list --parent <id>` correctly **excludes** deleted items.
- `render_report.py` (`render_from_wl`) counts `len(data["children"])` from `wl show --children`, so it **includes** the tombstones.

Observed on AH-0MUZMTTYH008KVS2: 7 active children + 6 soft-deleted coverage-gap children reported as `Children: 13`; `wl list --parent` correctly reports 7.

## Expected behaviour

The report's child count matches the active child set — i.e. it excludes items with `status=deleted` (or `deletedBy` set). Ideally the shared `wl show --children` behaviour and the report agree with `wl list --parent`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create a parent with children.
2. `wl delete <one-child> --json` (soft delete).
3. Run `python3 skill/report/scripts/render_report.py <parent-id> --skill-name plan ...`.
4. Observe the **Children** count includes the deleted child.

## Suggested fix

Filter deleted children in `render_from_wl` before counting (e.g. `[c for c in children if c.get("status") != "deleted" and not c.get("deletedBy")]`), or make `wl show --children` exclude deleted items consistently with `wl list --parent`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The report's **Children** count excludes soft-deleted items.
- A test covers a parent with a mix of active and soft-deleted children.
- Behaviour is consistent with `wl list --parent`.
data.title: Report script counts soft-deleted children

discovered-from:AH-0MUYRJQE50021T4A

## Problem

Several deterministic bot micro-simulations are knife-edge calibrations: a subtle, legitimate gameplay tweak (e.g. the 1-5% gentler thrust-press reduction in AH-0MUYRJQE50021T4A) flips their outcomes because scores are dominated by discrete hit/bullet collisions.

During AH-0MUYRJQE50021T4A two tests had to be recalibrated:
- src/ai/style/evaluation.test.ts - synthetic human seed moved 7 -> 14.
- src/ai/framework/competent/competentBot.integration.test.ts - RUN_SEED moved 0x0b07 -> 0x0b16.

On the base behaviour, src/ai/style/evaluation.test.ts already regressed on 13/24 seeds, and the competent-vs-legacy AC6 test only wins in base because the legacy bot chaotically collides with bullets; without bullets the legacy bot scored higher (22 vs 20) on base.

## Goal

Make these tests robust rather than seed-picked:
- Aggregate competence/style comparisons over a set of seeds (e.g. assert the styled/competent bot is not systematically worse), or
- Compare on scenarios whose score is not dominated by discrete collisions.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: The style-match AC4 demonstration no longer depends on a single lucky seed (e.g. asserts over multiple seeds).
- AC2: The competent-vs-legacy AC6 test asserts an objective-based advantage rather than relying on chaotic bullet collisions.
- AC3: Recalibrating either test is not required by an unrelated small bot-feel tweak.
- AC4: Full test suite, typecheck and build pass.
data.title: Make bot micro-simulation tests robust to small feel tweaks

# Centipede appears in the plain scenes column instead of ENEMIES (AH-0MV4ZOIZR0086T66)

## Problem statement

The dedicated `GymCentipede` enemy gym scene is discovered by the generic `Gym<Name>`
glob in `GymIndex` and rendered in the left-hand **plain scenes** column. The
Centipede is an enemy archetype, so it belongs in the middle **ENEMIES** column —
exactly where the analogous `GymBoss` scene already lives — so the index no longer
miscategorises an enemy testbed as a general-purpose scene.

## Users

- **Developer browsing the gym index** — expects enemy gym scenes to be grouped in the
  ENEMIES column so an enemy testbed is launched from the correct section.

### Example user stories

- As a **developer**, I want `GymCentipede` to appear in the **ENEMIES** column so that
  every enemy testbed is grouped together on the index.
- As a **developer**, I want `GymCentipede` to appear exactly once on the index (in the
  ENEMIES column, not the plain-scene column) so I don't see a confusing, miscategorised
  entry.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — `GymCentipede` removed from the plain scenes column:** `GymIndex.listedScenes`
      no longer contains `{ key: 'GymCentipede', label: 'Centipede' }`, and no `Centipede`
      text row is rendered at the plain-scenes column X (`GAME_WIDTH * GYM_INDEX_COLUMN_X.scenes`).
- [ ] **AC2 — `GymCentipede` surfaced as a dedicated ENEMIES row:** `GymIndex.listedEnemyScenes`
      contains `{ key: 'GymCentipede', label: 'Centipede', sceneKey: 'GymCentipede' }`, and a
      `Centipede` text row with `sceneKey === 'GymCentipede'` is rendered at the ENEMIES column X
      (`GAME_WIDTH * GYM_INDEX_COLUMN_X.enemies`), alongside the existing `Fodder Enemies` and
      `Boss` rows.
- [ ] **AC3 — The ENEMIES `Centipede` row launches `GymCentipede`:** pointer-click and
      keyboard (Enter/Space) activation of the row start the `GymCentipede` scene.
- [ ] **AC4 — Tests:** `GymIndex.test.ts` is updated so the plain-scene list expectation drops
      `Centipede` and new assertions cover the ENEMIES `Centipede` row (presence, column X,
      `sceneKey`, and launch). Every existing test continues to pass.
- [ ] **AC5 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes**, including code
      comments, `README.md`, and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`.
- [ ] **AC6 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Keep the three-column layout and the existing column X positions (`GYM_INDEX_COLUMN_X`)
  unchanged; this is a categorisation change only.
- Mirror the existing `GymBoss` exclusion/surfacing pattern in `GymIndex.ts`; do **not**
  introduce a new generic "auto-route every enemy gym to ENEMIES" mechanism (scope creep —
  see Risks).
- No behavioural change to `GymCentipede` itself (only its index visibility/labelling).
- Do **not** modify `src/utils/gymDiscovery.ts` — it stays a pure discovery helper; the
  column categorisation is owned by `GymIndex`.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/GymIndex.ts` builds `this.entries` from
  `discoverGymScenes(loadGymSceneModules())`, filtering out `GymFodderEnemies`, `GymBoss`
  and the Dev Utilities set (`DEV_UTILITY_SCENE_KEYS`). `GymCentipede` is **not** filtered,
  so it falls through into the left plain-scenes column.
- `this.enemyEntries` is currently hard-coded to `[Fodder Enemies, Boss]`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymCentipede.test.ts` asserts chain parity only; it does not assert index
  listing, so it needs no change.
- The Centipede is a **wave opt-in** (`centipede: true` in `PlayScene`), not a CSV enemy
  config, so it is not part of the `GymFodderEnemies` dropdown roster.

## Desired change

In `src/scenes/GymIndex.ts`:

1. Export `CENTIPEDE_SCENE_KEY = 'GymCentipede'` and `CENTIPEDE_LABEL = 'Centipede'`
   (mirroring `BOSS_SCENE_KEY` / `BOSS_SCENE_LABEL`).
2. Add `e.key !== CENTIPEDE_SCENE_KEY` to the `this.entries` filter so the scene is excluded
   from the plain scene list.
3. Add `{ key: CENTIPEDE_SCENE_KEY, label: CENTIPEDE_LABEL, sceneKey: CENTIPEDE_SCENE_KEY }`
   to `this.enemyEntries` (placed with the other dedicated scene rows).
4. Scene registration for `scene.start(key)` is already handled by the existing
   `for (const entry of all)` loop — no change required.
5. Update the module/class doc comments that enumerate the left-column exclusions so they
   include `GymCentipede`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/GymIndex.ts` — Add `CENTIPEDE_SCENE_KEY` / `CENTIPEDE_LABEL`; filter
  `GymCentipede` out of `this.entries`; append the dedicated ENEMIES row; update the
  module/class doc comments describing the columns.
- `src/scenes/GymIndex.test.ts` — Drop `Centipede` from the expected `listedScenes` list;
  assert the ENEMIES `Centipede` row (column X + `sceneKey` + launch); update the
  three-column layout test.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — §Gym surface: record that `GymCentipede` is
  surfaced in the ENEMIES column and excluded from the plain scene list.
- `README.md` — §Gym Index Entry Scene: ENEMIES column roster now reads
  `Fodder Enemies`, `Boss`, `Centipede`.

## Related work

- **Boss appears in both lists on index screen (AH-0MUAYB28C004KK7X)** — established the
  precedent: exclude an enemy scene from the plain-scene column and surface a dedicated
  ENEMIES row that boots the scene directly.
- **Single enemy gym scene with in-panel enemy selector dropdown (AH-0MV13G5EV008D41E)** —
  defines the three-column index layout and the ENEMIES column semantics.
- **Centipede segmented chain (AH-0MV01EJ92008ZZ86)** — created the `GymCentipede` scene.
- **Create Dev Utilities gym scene with curve editor and wave preview (AH-0MUGXDVPH005TIZL)** —
  sibling categorisation pattern (Dev Utilities column owns tooling scenes).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MTCNZ7DN0049K73** – Scene-level tests: GymPowerUps via gameHarness (completed)
- **AH-0MUE2MIXB007VOCY** – Documentation: README, ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION, code comments (completed)
- **AH-0MV2XDEKN0031KX4** – Test: gym parity intact (blocked)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: archetype, centipede, column, gym, scene (+34 more)
- `README.md` — matched: appears, archetype, centipede, column, enemies (+33 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: appears, archetype, centipede, column, currently (+30 more)

Full report: `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-AH-0MV4ZOIZR0086T66.md`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** "should be an enemy" means the `GymCentipede` **scene** belongs in the
  ENEMIES column, mirroring `GymBoss` — not that a `centipede` enemy config should be added
  to the fodder dropdown (the Centipede is a wave opt-in, not a CSV config).
- **Risk: Low.** A single-file categorisation change plus test/doc updates; no gameplay,
  entity or spawn behaviour changes.
- **Failure mode:** a `Centipede` label present in both the plain and ENEMIES columns would
  make the `findTextAt` label lookups in `GymIndex.test.ts` ambiguous — resolved by removing
  it from the plain list in the same change.
- **Scope-creep risk:** a general "auto-route every enemy gym scene to the ENEMIES column"
  mechanism is out of scope here; if wanted it should be captured as a separate work item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **No clarifying questions were required.** Research summary: the seed intent, combined
  with the existing `GymBoss` precedent (AH-0MUAYB28C004KK7X) and the documented three-column
  index contract (`src/scenes/GymIndex.ts`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`
  §"Gym surface", `README.md` §"Gym Index Entry Scene"), was sufficient to draft a clear
  brief. The one interpretation choice (dedicated ENEMIES **scene** row that boots
  `GymCentipede` directly, rather than adding a fodder-dropdown config) is recorded as an
  explicit documented assumption under Risks & assumptions.

# Implement GymPowerUpLeveling gym scene with integration tests

## Summary
Create a new auto-discovered gym scene `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts` that demonstrates the run-scoped power-up level curve for every power-up P3–P10, plus integration tests in `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.test.ts` that verify field-pickup leveling, hold-full permanent leveling, the level readout, and run-restart reset semantics.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Gym scene exists and is auto-discovered.** `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts` is created with class/scene key `GymPowerUpLeveling`, following the `Gym<Name>.ts` convention so `GymIndex` auto-discovers it without index edits.
- **AC2 — No duplicated model.** The gym reads levels and stats exclusively through `PowerUpLevelStore` and `resolvePowerUpAtLevel` from `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`. No copy of the curve, catalogue, level arithmetic, or shared helper is introduced. The duplicate-body guard in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` continues to pass.
- **AC3 — Every power-up P3–P10 is demonstrable.** The operator can collect each power-up repeatedly (field drops) and take a hold-full permanent reward. The scene shows the current run-scoped level plus the resolver-derived stats for all catalogue variables, updating visibly as the level rises.
- **AC4 — Integration tests.** `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.test.ts` drives the scene deterministically and verifies: field-pickup leveling, hold-full permanent leveling, the level readout matches `resolvePowerUpAtLevel` at representative levels (base / first upgrade / mid / cap), every P3–P10 has a growing axis, and the level resets only on run restart.
- **AC5 — Deterministic reset.** The gym exposes a public restart/reset hook so the reset test exercises `resetPowerUpLevels` without relying on a real GameOver sequence.

**Key Files:**

- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts` — **new** demonstration gym scene: round-robin/level-up drop source for P3–P10, hold-full permanent path, and a level + resolved-stats readout (reusing the shared store/resolver).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.test.ts` — **new** integration tests (field pickup, permanent reward, readout vs resolver, reset-on-restart, every-power-up-has-an-axis).
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — **read-only** shared source of truth (`POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS`, `resolvePowerUpAtLevel`, `PowerUpLevelStore`).
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — shared effect path consumed by the gym (read-only).
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — **read-only**; no changes to the shared HUD.

## Dependencies

- Parent work item provides the level model: AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6 (Design level curves for all power-ups).
- The effect path is wired by: AH-0MUV5CLW6005VF7K (Wire power-up level curves into EffectsRegistry), AH-0MUVM9RAO004Y3LB (Wire P3 shield absorption and P4 bomb axes), AH-0MUV5CLVO002ZHS9 (Integrate power-up level-up offers into the hold-full choice).
- Precedent: AH-0MUQOXHWT000XV4J (Weapon-leveling gym demonstration + integration tests).

## Deliverables

- GymPowerUpLeveling.ts gym scene
- GymPowerUpLeveling.test.ts integration tests
- No changes to shared model, HUD, or gameplay behaviour

# Game↔gym parity tests for the power-up level path

## Summary
Add parity tests that boot the **real** `GymPowerUpLeveling` gym alongside `PlayScene` and assert that, for every power-up P3–P10 across a level sweep (0, 1, mid, cap), the run-scoped level, resolved stats and observable effect-path outputs are identical. The parity assertion extends the shared equivalence/duplicate-body guard convention in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` (or a sibling parity test co-located with it).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Real-gym parity.** Tests boot the real `GymPowerUpLeveling` scene (not a minimal `EquivGymScene`) alongside `PlayScene` and assert identity of the shared power-up level path.
- **AC2 — Full coverage.** For every power-up P3–P10 and a level sweep (0, 1, mid, cap), the run-scoped level, resolved stats from `resolvePowerUpAtLevel`, and observable effect-path outputs (e.g. P5 speed multiplier, P8 lives, P3 absorptions, P7 teleports, P9/P10 stack caps) are identical between gym and game.
- **AC3 — Duplicate-body guard honoured.** The parity assertion lives in the shared equivalence test (or a sibling parity test) so the duplicate-body guard in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` remains the authoritative check; `GymPowerUpLeveling` introduces no divergent copy.
- **AC4 — Deterministic and efficient.** Tests drive `tick(dt)` only (no wall-clock); a single level sweep per power-up rather than many boots to keep parallel-suite runtime reasonable; generous Vitest timeouts for Phaser boot are acceptable.
- **AC5 — Threat handling is explicit.** If P3/P4/P6/P7 combat behaviour is required for the parity assertion, a threat toggle is added to the gym; otherwise the assertion covers the resolver/level/output path and documents that choice.

**Key Files:**

- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — extend (or add a sibling real-gym parity test) to boot `GymPowerUpLeveling` and assert `PlayScene`↔gym identity across every power-up and a level sweep.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts` — the real gym booted by the parity tests (read-only dependency; no changes unless the threat toggle is needed per AC5).
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — shared source of truth (read-only).

## Dependencies

- Depends on the gym scene existing (AH-0MV7QKEEO006WFI1) — the parity tests boot the real gym.
- Precedent: AH-0MUTPEIN0000MDUR (Test: P10 parity across PlayScene, GymMinerals and GymPowerUpsUtility — precedent for real-gym parity tests).
- Parent work item: AH-0MUV5CLVQ006V9HR.

## Deliverables

- Parity test code booting the real gym + PlayScene
- Full P3–P10 level-sweep coverage asserting identical level/stats/outputs
- Duplicate-body guard still passing
